utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You heard the question.

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: The question is clear. Articles of this kind with were very numerous. I can give you just one example that illustrates what those transcripts mean. In one of those transcripts that was also published by the weekly Nacional it was suggested that the former Minister of finances in cohorts with President Tudjman concealed 100 million dollars through the purchase of telecom of Croatia. Several days later that was proven false and was denied by the Minister of Finance. So there were articles of this kind in large numbers circulating in the Croatian media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Because of these and similar fictitious reports, did the President and the government pass this new law?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you the motives for the government to pass its decree but it was my feeling that the government was under great pressure of these pieces of paper that were being circulated and on the basis of these papers, some court proceedings have been instituted and all of them ended by being proven to be unfounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe that this testimony now about new laws or the new laws is beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, your objection is registered in the transcript. Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Mr. Pasalic, I don't wish to ask you any more questions except for this one last question. Tell me, please, I have looked through the transcripts disclosed to me, and that I have seen that pages are missing in many of them. Is it possible for pages to be missing and not to be in order? And is it possible for anyone to write down anything on these transcripts in free hand?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, that is absolutely --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the question. I believe it's beyond the scope of cross. It's also something that was gone into on direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's out of the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in view of the fact that the Prosecutor spent an hour discussing P14 and read out the transcript, to refresh the memory of the witness, my final question:

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please look at page 03 -- oh, you don't have it in front of you. Tell me, please, finally, and once and for all, were you at this meeting? Can you now remember, after this hour of refreshing your memory, were you at that meeting? And after the words uttered by the President in that have no meaning in the context, do you remember yourself saying at that meeting, according to this transcript that we have been listening to for an hour, with Mato and you, we don't know who the "you" is, it cannot be seen from the transcript, "He is the most prominent person from that area in the Croatian media." It is page 7038. It is out of context entirely that you utter this sentence. Did you say that?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: All I can say is something similar to what I answered to the Prosecutor, that after a whole series of events that are described in this document, and everything that is said there, I can only repeat that I would certainly have remembered if I had attended such a meeting, and after all the details presented, I am quite sure that I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, who, then produced this transcript?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: I'm unable to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seric?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher once again give the witness document PT14, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Dr. Pasalic, will you please look at this transcript, page 1? When was -- did this alleged meeting actually begin?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: It says at 9.30 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now look at the last page, please. When did it end?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: It says here that the meeting ended at 10.55.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Can you quickly work out how long the meeting lasted?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: According to this transcript, one hour 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Could you read the top number on -- in the right-hand corner? How many pages were there. The first page is 014 and it ends 072. So that would be about 58 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: According to your own experience, as you attended many political meetings, is it possible for so much to have been said in one hour 25 minutes? As we see on more than 50 pages?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Meetings of that kind, with so much text, would normally last much longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Will you please look at the page 023? The last digits being 023?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the top left-hand corner, we have some numbers again.

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Yes 2/6, LJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Now, next page, what do you see there?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: It says 3/1/JG.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And the end of the text on the previous page, does the text follow on to that text?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: As far as I'm able to judge, the end of the text on page 023 does not seem to be logically connected to what we find on page 024.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Please look at page 028. Last three digits?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And the next one is 029. In the top left-hand corner are numbers missing?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: 028, we have the upper left-hand corner, in the left?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: In the upper left-hand corner we see 3/5/JG.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And on the next page?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: On the next page, 4/1/LJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Then look at page 032, please.

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: Yes. I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the top left-hand corner, what numbers do you see?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: And on the next page?

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: On the next page, we have 5/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Then look at page 038, please.

utterances.speaker: IVIC PASALIC
utterances.text: 038, yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: In the top left-hand corner, what are the numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Next page?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: Let's go on. Page 044.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Seric, it's not necessary to point every place that is inconsistent. Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President, I won't go any further. I just want the witness to see that a whole series of pages are missing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, --

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And that the text does not have continuity. Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The purpose is to let us see. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President, sit setting aside whether one can have a redirect when one never had a direct, I just want to bring the Trial Chamber's attention to the fact that the notations on the upper left-hand corner are addressed in transcript testimony that's been presented to the Trial Chamber earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Very clearly explained, I might say so. So Dr. Seric you might read these transcripts and you might know exactly what those mean. It was explained by the people who prepared the documents exactly what those letters meant, they are to do with the tapes and the people who typed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SERIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour, I just wanted to say that my learned friend is not right. These are joint witnesses. I allowed my colleague Krsnik to question him simply to gain time. So he's not right in saying I have no -- I'm not entitled to redirect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This Trial Chamber has noticed that. That's why we allowed you to re-examine this witness. Witness, thank you very much for coming here to give your evidence. We appreciate it very much. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. Could I give you a piece of advice? If in the future you have another chance to be in The Hague to be a witness, do not talk to any person from the media and do not get in touch with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it was a pleasure to testify here. If I might -- if I may just make a brief explanation, I'm a member of parliament of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We quite understand that. It's just my advice to you. You may take it or not. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: As for the documents tendered, I hope both parties will submit a list for the documents they are going to tender for this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are at a very late hour. At this moment I would like to thank the interpreters, the court reporters and all the security people for their cooperation. We'll make the time up. Maybe for the next sitting. Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank this honourable Trial Chamber for allowing the witness to go home. I'm most grateful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll resume tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 8.01 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 11th day of June, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
